{{Short description|1997 single by Wyclef Jean}} {{distinguish|Gone 'Til November|Gone till November (Rod Wave song)}} {{More citations needed|date=June 2015}} {{Use dmy dates|date=May 2021}} {{Infobox song | name = Gone till November | cover = Gonetillnovember.jpg | alt = Jean playing guitar onstage | type = single | artist = [[Wyclef Jean]] | album = [[Wyclef Jean Presents The Carnival|The Carnival]] | B-side = No Airplay | released = {{start date|1997|11|25|df=y}} | recorded = | studio = | venue = | genre = | length = {{Duration|m=3|s=28}} | label = [[Columbia Records|Columbia]], [[Ruffhouse Records|Ruffhouse]] | writer = Wyclef Jean, [[Jerry Duplessis]] | producer = Wyclef Jean, Jerry "Wonda" Duplessis | prev_title = [[No, No, No (Destiny's Child song)|No, No, No]] | prev_year = 1997 | next_title = [[Cheated (To All the Girls)]] | next_year = 1998 }} "'''Gone till November'''" a song by Haitian [[rapping|rapper]] [[Wyclef Jean]], released as the third single from his debut solo album ''[[Wyclef Jean Presents The Carnival|The Carnival]]'' (1997). The song was released on 25 November 1997 by [[Columbia Records|Columbia]] and [[Ruffhouse Records|Ruffhouse]], and peaked at number three on the [[UK Singles Chart]], becoming Jean's highest-charting solo hit in the UK alongside 2000's "[[It Doesn't Matter (Wyclef Jean song)|It Doesn't Matter]]". In the United States, the song peaked at number seven on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] chart. It reached number four in both Canada and New Zealand. The album version differs from the more-familiar pop version found on the single and used in the video. The album version has a different bass line and more, different, voiceover. The pop version is more recognizable due to radio play but is not found on the actual album. Both album and pop versions differ from the "remix" version. ==Composition== The orchestral accompaniment, which was arranged and conducted by Sonny Kompanek, was performed by the [[New York Philharmonic Orchestra]]. ==Chart performance== "Gone till November" peaked at number seven on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] and spent a total of 20 weeks on the chart. It also peaked at number nine on the US [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs]] chart. In the UK, the song debuted at number three on the [[UK Singles Chart]] and spent a total of nine weeks on the chart. This became Wyclef's highest-charting single on the chart. The single was eventually certified [[RIAA Certification|platinum]] by the [[Recording Industry Association of America]] (RIAA) for sales of over a million copies in the United States. ==Critical reception== British magazine ''[[Music Week]]'' wrote, "This laidback ode to a footloose lifestyle by [[the Fugees]] rapper is desperately catchy and features pleasing arrangements, but somehow seems a bit lifeless."{{cite magazine|first=|last=|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/UK/Music-Week/1998/Music-Week-1998-04-04.pdf|title=Single reviews|magazine=[[Music Week]]|date=April 4, 1998|page=10|access-date=September 15, 2023}} ==Remix== The remix of "Gone till November" features [[R. Kelly]] and [[Canibus]], with backing vocals by Destiny's Child, and contains interpolations of the songs "[[Michelle (song)|Michelle]]" by [[the Beatles]] and "[[Karma Chameleon]]" by [[Culture Club]]. A separate music video was also made for the remix version. ==Music video== The music video for "Gone till November", directed by [[Francis Lawrence]], was filmed at [[Los Angeles International Airport]] (LAX) on 20 November 1997, and released in December 1997.{{Cite web |author=MTV News Staff |date=December 22, 1997 |title=Bob Dylan Makes Cameo In Wyclef Video |url=https://www.mtv.com/news/1428462/bob-dylan-makes-cameo-in-wyclef-video/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170422133359/http://www.mtv.com/news/1428462/bob-dylan-makes-cameo-in-wyclef-video/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=22 April 2017 |access-date=2022-04-30 |website=MTV News |language=en}} It features a [[cameo appearance]] by [[Bob Dylan]] when Wyclef sings, "[[knockin' on heaven's door]] like I'm Bob Dylan."{{cite magazine|last=Nelson|first=Havelock|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0g0EAAAAMBAJ&pg=RA1-PA85|title=The Rap Column|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=27 December 1997|page=85|access-date=22 July 2013}}{{cite magazine|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-Billboard/90s/1998/BB-1998-02-07.pdf|title=Production Notes|magazine=Billboard|volume=110|issue=6|page=86|date=7 February 1998|access-date=17 October 2020}} [[Canibus]] and [[Destiny's Child]] also make appearances respectively, but R.
